(a) As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the following meanings:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine, or fortified wine as defined in this section.
Ancillary retailer means a for-profit business or nonprofit organization located within the city that is licensed under this chapter to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises as an incidental use to its primary business purpose. Examples of ancillary retailers include, but are not limited to, art galleries, museums, theaters, dog parks, entertainment venues, and similar establishments. An ancillary retailer shall not derive more than twenty (20) percent of its total annual gross revenue from the sale of alcoholic beverages.
Brewery means any establishment where malt beverages are manufactured.
Brewpub means any eating establishment in which malt beverages are manufactured, subject to the barrel production limitation prescribed in O.C.G.A. § 3-5-36. As used in this paragraph, the term "eating establishment" means an establishment which is licensed to sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wines and which derives at least fifty (50) percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food; provided, however, that when determining the total annual gross food and beverage sales, barrels of malt beverages sold to licensed wholesale dealers, as authorized pursuant to subparagraph (D) of paragraph (2) of O.C.G.A. § 3-5-36, or to the public for consumption off the premises, as authorized pursuant to subparagraph (D) of paragraph (2) and paragraph (4) of O.C.G.A. § 3-5-36, shall not be used.
Brown-bagging means the bringing, taking, or carrying of any alcoholic beverage into:
(1) An establishment that does not have an alcohol license for the consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises; or
(2) Where said individual in possession of the alcoholic beverage does not have a caterer's license; provided that bringing an alcoholic beverage into a house, apartment, room, or other unit designed for private residential occupancy shall not fall within this definition.
City means the City of Forest Park, Georgia.
Complimentary service means the gratuitous provision of malt beverages or wine to patrons in connection with services provided by a business, including but not limited to salons, barbershops, spas, or similar establishments, pursuant to a license issued under this chapter.
Craft beer means a malt beverage produced by a brewery whose annual production does not exceed six million (6,000,000) barrels of beer and whose flavor is derived primarily from traditional or innovative brewing ingredients and the fermentation process.
Craft beer and wine market means a retail establishment that derives at least seventy (70) percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of craft beer, hard cider, wine, or a combination thereof, and which is licensed under this chapter to sell such beverages in accordance with applicable law.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than twenty-four (24) percent alcohol by volume.
Eating establishment or restaurant means any public place, including a place available for rental by the public, that is open to the public, licensed to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, and derives at least fifty (50) percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food. An eating establishment shall maintain a full-service kitchen consisting of, at a minimum, a stove or grill, refrigeration equipment, and a three-compartment sink, all of which shall be maintained in good working order and approved by the applicable health and fire authorities. Food shall be available for service during all hours alcoholic beverages are offered for sale, except during temporary interruptions due to emergencies, repairs, or circumstances beyond the control of the licensee.
Farm winery means a winery that produces wine from agricultural products and satisfies the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1, as may be amended from time to time. In the event of a conflict between this chapter and state law, the definition set forth in O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1 shall control.
Farm winery tasting room means a facility operated by or on behalf of a farm winery for the promotion, sampling, tasting, sale, and distribution of wine in accordance with applicable state law. A farm winery tasting room may provide wine samples to the public, with or without charge, and may sell wine for on-premises consumption or in closed containers for off-premises consumption as authorized by state law.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing more than twenty-one (21) percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added, including, but not limited to, brandy.
Gallon or wine gallon means a United States gallon of liquid measurement equivalent to the volume of two hundred thirty-one (231) cubic inches or the nearest equivalent metric measurement.
Growler means a container that is filled by a licensee or employee of a licensee with beer or wine from a barrel, keg, or cask for off premises consumption.
Hard cider means an alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of the juice of apples, containing not more than six (6) percent alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, flavored or carbonated cider. For purposes of this chapter, hard cider shall be deemed a malt beverage. The term "hard cider" does not include "sweet cider."
Hotel/motel means any building or group of buildings operated as a unified business providing sleeping accommodations for compensation to the general public. To qualify under this chapter, a hotel or motel shall maintain a minimum of fifty (50) guest rooms available for occupancy and shall contain at least one (1) public dining facility with an adequate kitchen approved by the applicable health and fire authorities. Hotels and motels may include restaurants, lounges, bars, or other food and beverage operations located within the premises and operated by the hotel, motel, or an authorized franchisee or concessionaire.
Importer means any person who imports an alcoholic beverage into the State of Georgia and or the city from a foreign country who maintains a stock of such alcoholic beverages and sells the alcoholic beverages to another importer, or a broker, or wholesaler.
Individual means a natural person.
License means an authorization granted by the city to operate as one (1) of the classes of licenses described in section 9-2-3(c) of this chapter.
License representative means an individual designated by a licensee to act on behalf of the licensee with respect to matters arising under this chapter, including communications with the city, regulatory compliance, inspections, investigations, and enforcement proceedings.
Licensee means the individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity to whom a license is issued pursuant to this chapter and who shall be responsible for compliance with all applicable provisions of this chapter and state law governing alcoholic beverages.
Malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than fourteen (14) percent alcohol by volume and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Manufacturer means any maker, producer, or bottler of an alcoholic beverage, and shall also include:
(1) In the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits;
(2) In the case of malt beverages, any brewer;
(3) In the case of wine, any vintner.
Microbrewery is the term used in this chapter to collectively refer to breweries and brewpubs.
Micro-distillery means an establishment in which not more than ten thousand (10,000) barrels of distilled spirits are manufactured on the licensed premises during a calendar year and in which such distilled spirits may be sold for on-premises consumption and off-premises consumption to the extent authorized by state law. As used herein, the term "barrel" shall have the meaning prescribed by the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code.
Open alcoholic beverage container means any bottle, can, or other receptacle that:
(1) Contains any amount of alcoholic beverage; and
(2) Is open, has a broken seal, or the contents of which have been partially removed.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container. Retail package alcoholic beverages shall include all alcoholic beverages in their original container, sold at retail to the final consumer, and not for resale.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Pouring/alcohol permit means an authorization granted to individuals by the city to dispense, sell, serve, take orders, or mix alcoholic beverages.
Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, at retail, only to consumers and not for resale.
Retail package dealer means any person who sells unbroken packages, at retail, only to consumers and not for resale.
Special event means a temporary activity, gathering, festival, concert, exhibition, fundraiser, celebration, competition, market, or similar event conducted at a fixed location for a limited duration and authorized by the city, at which alcoholic beverages may be sold, served, dispensed, possessed, or consumed pursuant to a special event license or permit issued under this chapter.
Ticketed event means an event conducted at a licensed premises for which admission is conditioned upon the purchase, possession, or presentation of a ticket, pass, wristband, reservation, or similar authorization for entry.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail package dealers, or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than twenty-four (24) percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this code section.

(1) Applicant. Any individual applying for any license authorized by this article on an application form supplied by the city for such purpose.

(3) Premises. The interior portion of any improvement situated at the address of a licensee under this chapter, and in the case of a licensee authorized to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises may include an outdoor patio that provides tables and seating for a minimum of fifteen (15) persons.

d. (5) Private residence. Any structure(s) designed or intended for permanent dwelling by people.

(a) All applications for licenses under this chapter shall be made on forms furnished by the city and shall indicate, along with all information reasonably necessary to complete the form, which license is being applied for under section 9-2-3(c)(1) through (27) above.
(b) Upon approval of an original or renewal application for a license of one (1) of the above type sales of alcoholic beverages, such sales may be made by the applicant after a license is issued for all the remaining part of a calendar year, unless the same is suspended or revoked for due cause as provided hereinafter.
(c) Any and all licenses granted under this chapter shall expire on December 31 of each year. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file an application, with the requisite fee provided for in this chapter, with the city's director of finance or his designee, on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. Applications for renewal must be filed on or before October 1 of each year; with all fees paid no later than November 15 of each year. Otherwise, a late charge of ten (10) percent, plus interest at the rate set forth in subsection (d) shall be assessed thereafter. No renewal license shall be granted after the previous license has expired on December 31, and any application submitted thereafter shall be treated as an initial application and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been held. All licenses granted under this chapter shall be for the calendar year or for the number of months remaining in the calendar year, and shall expire on December 31 of each calendar year. License fees shall be prorated based on the number of months remaining in the calendar year, and partial months shall be counted as a full month. License fees are not refundable.
(d) Any person renewing any license issued under this chapter who shall pay the required fee, or any portion thereof, after the date set forth in this chapter for such payment, shall, in addition to the annual fee, pay a late charge of ten (10) percent, and shall also pay simple interest on the delinquent balance at the annual rate then charged by the Internal Revenue Service of the United States on unpaid federal income taxes.
(e) No application will be considered from any applicant who, either individually or in association with any other person or party, shall have at the time any outstanding taxes, fees, special assessments, or any other sums that are due and owing to the city. Further, no application shall be given to any person who does not possess an occupational tax certificate issued by the city, and all applicants shall submit a copy of their most current occupational tax certificate with their application. Any application issued or considered and/or approved contrary to the requirements stated in this subsection, shall be considered and declared null and void, and any and all monies paid by the applicant shall be returned to the applicant.
(f) All applicants, by filing any application with the city, do by such filing authorize and give consent to the city's police department to make full and complete investigations into all persons, corporations, or other entities named in such application, and into any person who shall have an interest in any license issued hereunder, and any information sought or required by such department shall be readily furnished by such applicant, and no license shall be considered until such information as requested by such department has been satisfactorily furnished.

1090:
The sale of any alcoholic beverage to any person under the minimum legal age established by the laws of the State of Georgia, or to any person in an apparent intoxicated condition, or to any person known to the licensee or his agent to be a habitual drunkard, is hereby prohibited. The solicitation of any such purchase by any minor, or the misrepresentation of any such minor as to his age, is likewise prohibited.
No holder or employee of the holder of a license authorizing the sale of alcoholic beverages, shall do any of the following upon the licensed premises:
(1) Sell or offer to sell any distilled spirits, wines, malt beverages, or any other alcoholic beverage to any person under the age of twenty-one (21) years.
(2) The prohibition in subsection (1) of this section shall not apply with respect to the sale of alcoholic beverages to a person when such person has furnished proper identification showing that the person to whom the alcoholic beverages are being sold is twenty-one (21) years of age or older. For the purposes of this subsection, proper identification means any document issued by a government agency containing a description of the person, such person's photograph, or both, and giving such person's date of birth, including, but not limited to, a passport, military identification card, driver's license, or identification card authorized under an act to require the department of public safety to issue identification cards to persons who do not have a motor vehicle driver's license. Proper identification shall not include a birth certificate.
(3) Sell or offer to sell any alcoholic beverages to any person who is noticeably intoxicated, who is of unsound mind, or who is a habitual drunkard whose intemperate habits are known to the licensee or his employees.
(4) Sell alcoholic beverages upon the licensed premises or permit alcoholic beverages to be consumed thereon, on any day or at any time when the sale or consumption is prohibited by state law or city ordinance.
(5) No person who holds a license to sell alcoholic beverages by the drink shall allow any minors to be in, frequent or loiter about the licensed premises of the establishment or lounge unless such minors are accompanied by a parent, legal guardian, or custodian; provided, however, that such minors shall be permitted in eating establishments, private clubs, hotels, entertainment venues, ancillary retailers or other establishments specifically authorized under this chapter without being accompanied by a parent, legal guardian, or custodian and provided further that this section shall not apply to minors who are employees under the terms of this chapter.
(6) The penalty for violation of this section by an individual shall be as follows:
a. For the first offense, a minimum fine of five hundred dollars ($500.00).
b. For the second offense and subsequent violations within one (1) year, a minimum fine of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
(7) Any licensed establishment where two (2) or more violations of this section, or O.C.G.A. § 3-3-23 and related regulations have occurred within any twenty-four-month period shall be punished as follows:
a. For the second offense within any twenty-four-month period, suspension of license(s) for a period not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days.
b. For the third and any subsequent violation within any twenty-four-month period, suspension of license(s) for a period not to exceed one (1) year.
As to the penalties in this subsection, if there is a change in a majority of the licensed establishment's owners, partners or shareholders, the violations under the old ownership shall not count against the new owners; however, a different corporation, partnership or other association will be charged with the violations of its predecessor(s) if a majority of the owners, partners or shareholders are the same.
(8) A conviction shall not be required for the city to pursue administrative suspension, revocation, or other enforcement remedies authorized by this chapter.
(Ord. No. 12-33, § 1, 9-17-2012; Ord. No. 26-16, § 1(Exh. A), 8-3-2026)

1093:
The following regulations shall apply to all establishments holding a license for consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises:
(1) No person shall be employed to dispense, sell, serve, take orders, mix alcoholic beverages, or serve in any managerial position, by an establishment holding a license under this chapter until such person has been approved by the chief of police or his designee, indicating that the person is eligible for such employment.
(2) This section shall not be construed to include volunteer groups with non-profit tax exempt status from the Internal Revenue Service whose volunteer efforts financially benefit a non-profit organization with no direct financial benefit, either by wages, tips or donations, to the individual volunteer. No volunteer under the age of eighteen (18) shall be allowed to dispense, sell, serve, take orders or mix alcoholic beverages. Employees of a licensed establishment whose duties are limited solely to those of busboy(s), cook(s), or dishwasher(s) shall also be excluded from this section.
(3) No permit shall be issued until such time as a signed application has been filed with the chief of police or his designee, and upon paying a fee as established by the governing body by resolution from time to time and kept on file in the office of the director of finance, and a search of the criminal record of the applicant completed. The application shall include, but shall not be limited to, the name, date of birth, current address, and such other information as may be reasonably required by the chief of police or his designee to determine eligibility for a permit under this chapter. The applicant shall authorize the city to conduct such criminal history and background investigations as may be reasonably necessary to determine eligibility for a permit under this chapter.
(4) The chief of police or his designee shall have a complete and exhaustive search made relative to any police record of the person fingerprinted or cleared. If there is no record of a violation of this chapter, the chief of police or his designee shall issue a permit to the person, in person, stating, in writing, that the person is eligible for employment. If it is found that the person is not eligible for employment, the chief of police or his designee shall notify the person, in writing, that they are not eligible for employment, the cause of such denial and their right to appeal.
(5) No person shall be granted a permit under this chapter unless it appears to the satisfaction of the chief of police or his designee, that such person has not been convicted or pled guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any crime involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling, or illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or the illegal sale or possession of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in a manner contrary to law, keeping a place of prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexual related crime within a period of ten (10) years of the date of conviction and has been released from parole or probation. A person's first time conviction for illegal possession of alcohol as a misdemeanor or violation of a city or county ordinance shall not, by itself, make a person ineligible for an alcohol permit. No person shall be granted a permit under this chapter who has been convicted, plead guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any federal, state, or local law for any felony within five (5) years of the date of conviction and has not been released from parole or probation prior to the filing for application for such permit. A discharge pursuant to the Georgia First Offender Act shall not constitute a conviction unless an adjudication of guilt has subsequently been entered. Except, however, that any such offense shall not be ignored where the defendant violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting the first offender treatment or committed another crime and the sentence in court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which the defendant had previously been sentenced as a first offender.
(6) An alcohol/pouring permit shall be issued for a period of one (1) calendar year from the date of the original application. This permit must be worn by the employee while the permit holder is working and available for inspection by members of the police department or the code enforcement department. The permit holder shall maintain proof of a valid permit and present such proof upon request of any authorized city official.
(7) No person shall be issued a permit if it is determined that the person falsified, concealed or covered up any material fact by any device, trick or scheme while making application to the police department for an alcohol/pouring permit under this section.
If it is determined that a person is in violation of this subsection and a permit is denied for this reason, then sixty (60) calendar days must elapse from the date of notification per regular U.S. mail to the address on file for the person, before a new application and fee may be resubmitted.
(8) All permits issued through administrative error can be terminated and seized by the chief of police or his designee, or code enforcement.
(9) Replacement permits will be issued within thirty (30) days of the original date, upon paying one-half of the fees charged for alcohol/pouring permits. After thirty (30) days of the original application date, a new application and fee must be submitted.
(10) All permits issued under this chapter remain the property of the police department and shall be produced for inspection upon the demand of any officer or designee of the police department or employee of the business license department or code enforcement department.
(11) No licensee shall allow any employee or manager required to hold a permit to work on the premises unless the employee or manager has in their possession a current valid city pouring permit. For new employees, a receipt issued by the chief of police permit unit may be used for a maximum of thirty (30) days from the date of its issue. Licensees are required by this chapter to inspect and verify that each employee required to do so, has in his possession a valid current alcohol permit. This requirement shall apply to all licensees and all employees working in any retail establishment engaged in the retail sale of alcoholic beverages, by the package or for consumption on the premises.
(12) Each licensee shall maintain current records identifying all employees required to hold permits under this chapter and shall make such records available to the city upon reasonable request.
(13) Any person(s) convicted of any violation(s) of this section shall receive a minimum fine of three hundred dollars ($300.00).

Any person violating any section of this chapter shall be subject to the general penalty provided in section 1-1-8 of this Code, and, in addition, shall be subject to revocation of their license to do business as a pawnbroker in this city. Any person violating any provision of this chapter shall be subject to the general penalty provided in section 1-1-8 of this Code. Each day that a violation of this chapter exists shall constitute a separate offense. In addition to any criminal penalties, a violation of this chapter shall constitute grounds for denial, suspension, or revocation of a pawnbroker's license.
(Code 1959, § 12A-12; Ord. No. 26-06, § 2(Exh. B), 5-4-2026; Ord. No. 26-15, § 2(Exh. B), 8-3-2026)
1171:
(a) If the city is authorized to issue an additional pawnbroker license due to population increase, revocation, surrender, or other availability, the city manager shall cause notice of such availability to be published in the legal organ of Clayton County. Such notice shall include the following:
(1) That the city has the ability to issue a pawnbrokers license.
(2) That any party wishing to apply for said license shall make application to the city for same within thirty (30) days of the date of publication of the notice.
(3) All applications shall be reviewed and approved as qualifying for the license as provided for in section 9-3-3 of this Code.
(4) The city manager shall notify applicants who meet the minimum qualifications that they are eligible for consideration for issuance of a license. Each such applicant shall submit the required license fee within seventy-two (72) hours of notification. Failure to timely submit the required fee shall result in removal of the applicant from further consideration.
(b) If the number of qualified applicants exceeds the number of available licenses, the city manager shall conduct a random selection process at a publicly noticed meeting to determine which applicant or applicants shall receive a license.
(c) Application fees paid by applicants not selected shall be refunded.
(d) By submitting an application pursuant to this section, each applicant acknowledges that the issuance of a pawnbroker license is a privilege and not a right, and that the selection process shall be conducted in accordance with this section.
(Ord. No. 94-005, 12-19-94; Ord. No. 26-06, § 2(Exh. B), 5-4-2026; Ord. No. 26-15, § 2(Exh. B), 8-3-2026)
1172: Editor's note— Ord. No. 26-06, § 2(Exh. B), adopted May 4, 2026, repealed § 9-3-14, which pertained to moratorium on the licensing of pawnbrokers and derived from Ord. No. 98-002, § I, adopted Feb. 26, 1998.
1173:
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Code, a pawnbroker duly licensed and in good standing with the city may request approval to transfer such license to another person, subject to the requirements of this section:
(1) The license holder shall submit written notice to the mayor and council of the intent to transfer the license, together with a completed application for the proposed transferee, including all information and documentation required for an original license application.
(2) The chief of police shall review and investigate the application of the proposed transferee using the same standards applicable to an original license application and shall provide a recommendation to the mayor and council for approval or denial.
(3) Upon approval by the mayor and council, and upon payment of the required license fee, the city clerk shall issue a license to the approved transferee.
(b) Any material misrepresentation or omission in the application of the proposed transferee shall be grounds for denial of the transfer request and may constitute grounds for suspension or revocation of the existing license.
(Ord. No. 98-010, § 1, 6-15-98; Ord. No. 26-06, § 2(Exh. B), 5-4-2026; Ord. No. 26-15, § 2(Exh. B), 8-3-2026)

1175:
The term "wrecker" as used in this chapter means any vehicle equipped and used for the purpose of towing wrecked or disabled automobiles or vehicles; and the term "wrecker service" shall mean any person, firm, partnership, or corporation which is engaged solely or partially in the business of towing wrecked or disabled automobiles or vehicles.
(Code 1959, § 23A-1(a))
1176:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation, either as principal, agent or employee, to use or operate upon any of the streets of the city or any area inside the corporate limits, any wrecker without complying with the provisions of this chapter except as provided herein.
(Code 1959, § 23A-1(b))
1177:
It shall be unlawful for any person, partnership, firm, association, or corporation to operate or cause to be operated, any wrecker, as defined in section 9-4-1 within the corporate limits of the city, which maintains its principal, or any branch office within the corporate city limits, or any wrecker services which generates 50 percent of its gross income by conducting business within the corporate city limits, without first having obtained a business license from the revenue collection division of the city.
(Code 1959, § 23A-2)
State Law reference— Municipal license fees and business taxes on wrecker services limited, O.C.G.A., § 48-13-10.1.
1178:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or cause to be operated, a wrecker as defined in subsection 9-4-1, unless the wrecker bears a current registered decal. The decal shall be valid for a period of one (1) year from date of issue and shall bear the registration decal number, the date of issue and the date of expiration, together with any other information deemed appropriate by the chief of police or his delegate. The decal shall be placed on the lower corner of the windshield of the wrecker on the driver's side.
(Code 1959, § 23A-3)
1179:
(a) No business license shall be required for any wrecker or wrecker service which is operated within the city when the wrecker company is duly licensed and registered in accordance with the laws, if any, of the place having jurisdiction over the business.
(b) Any wrecker, or wrecker service, which uses the streets of the city, for purposes of either point of pickup of a motor vehicle or point of delivery of same on a regular basis, shall be required to obtain and display a registration decal as provided in sections 9-4-4 and 9-4-6 of this chapter. A "regular basis" shall be defined for purposes of this chapter as meaning more than one time in a calendar year.
(c) The wrecker or wrecker service is not engaged in any activity whereby neither the point of pickup or the point of delivery of any wrecked or disabled vehicle is within the city, or otherwise does not engage in business in the city; provided, that the burden is upon the wrecker, wrecker service, or his agent to prove either the point of pickup or the point of delivery is not within the city limits; specifically a wrecker or wrecker service which merely passes through the city limits is exempt from complying with the terms of this chapter.
(Code 1959, § 23A-4)
1180:
Application for the registration decal required by section 9-4-4 shall be made to the inspection and permits unit of the city police department on forms prescribed and provided by that department. The application form, which shall be completed under oath, shall contain the name, address and telephone number of any person, partnership, firm, association or corporation operating or causing the operation of the wrecker; the name, address and telephone number of the owner of the wrecker, if different from the operator; the make, model, color, year of manufacture, tag number and vehicle identification number of the wrecker; the date the wrecker was put into service; the state emergency light permit number; and the business license number, if any, and the name and policy number of the casualty insurance carrier covering said vehicle.
(Code 1959, § 23A-5)
1181:
It shall be unlawful for any person, partnership, firm, association or corporation, either as principal, agent or employee, to operate or cause to be operated within the city any wrecker as defined in section 9-4-1, unless this vehicle shall have lettered in permanent paint on each side in plain view the following information: the name of the person, partnership, firm, association or corporation owning and causing its wrecker to operate on the streets of the city, the address from which the wrecker is operating and the telephone number. This lettering shall be in contrasting color to the color of the wrecker and shall be at least two and one half (2-½) inches in height. Temporary or removable magnetic signs shall not be permitted.
(Code 1959, § 23A-6)
1182:
(a) Wrecker services; storage facilities. The owner or operator of any business providing wrecker service or storage facilities for vehicles shall furnish to the criminal investigation division of the police department, on forms of the type approved by the department, a typed, weekly report listing all motor vehicles towed or stored within the city and remaining within the possession of the business on the Friday following the towing or storage. The vehicle shall be listed in each subsequent weekly report so long as it remains in the possession of the business.
(b) Auto salvage; crushing businesses; junk yards. Any person, partnership, firm, association or corporation in the business of auto salvage or otherwise in the business of selling used parts from vehicles within the seller's possession and any person, partnership, firm, association or corporation in the business of crushing, cutting up or otherwise permanently destroying vehicles for scrap metal shall furnish to the criminal investigation division of the police department, on forms of a type approved by the department, a typed, weekly report listing all vehicles obtained for the purpose of salvage, used parts, or scrap metal, during the weekly reporting period. The weekly reporting period shall begin at 12:01 a.m. each Saturday.
(c) Contents of report. The weekly reports required by subsections (a) and (b) shall be due each Tuesday and shall contain the name of the person, partnership, firm, association, or corporation reporting; the authority under which the vehicle was towed, stored or salvaged for parts or scrap metal; a description of the vehicle; the location of its present storage site, if applicable its tag number, if any; its year and make; its color; and its vehicle identification number.
(d) Inability to obtain information without damaging vehicle. If any of the information required by subsection (c) cannot be obtained for the weekly report required by subsection (a) without damaging the vehicle, the fact shall be conveyed by the owner or operator of the wrecker service or storage facility to the police department by telephonic communication and shall also be set forth in the weekly report.
(Code 1959, § 23A-7)
1183:
It shall be unlawful for the owner of any wrecker, or his agent, representative or employee, to go to any place where an accident has occurred unless called by the driver or the owner of the disabled vehicle or the owner's authorized representative, or by the police division dispatcher. It shall be unlawful for the owner of any wrecker, or his agent, representative or employee to go to the place of the wreck by reason of information received by police radio.
(Code 1959, § 23A-8)
1184:
All wrecker operators, after having been called to the scene of an accident for the purpose of removing a damaged vehicle, shall clean all debris caused by the accident from the street and right-of-way before they leave. In the event two (2) or more wreckers are called to the same accident, they shall be equally responsible for cleaning.
(Code 1959, § 23A-9)
State Law reference— Similar requirement under state law, O.C.G.A., § 40-6-277.
1185:
It shall be unlawful for any city employee to solicit business for any wrecker owner or operator.
(Code 1959, § 23A-10)
1186:
It shall be unlawful to cruise or park on any street or bridge in a wrecker and solicit towing work.
(Code 1959, § 23A-11)
1187:
(a) The chief of police, or his delegate, may petition the city business license section to revoke the business license and recall and cancel the decals of any wrecker or owner or operator when he has been found in violation of any of the terms of this chapter or upon any of the following grounds:
(1) if the registration was procured by fraudulent conduct or false statement of a material fact as to ownership, use, possession or operation;
(2) if the owner or licensee is found at the scene of an accident in violation of the provisions of this chapter;
(3) if the licensee uses a police radio to obtain information as to the location of the scene of the accident; or
(4) if the licensee shall pay in the form of gratuity any person not involved in the accident for information as to the location of the accident.
(b) This revocation shall terminate all authority and permission granted by the registration to the wrecker owner. Any person whose registration has been revoked shall not be eligible to again apply for a license for a period of one (1) year from the date of issuance of the original license.
(c) Any person whose license has been revoked or decal has been cancelled by the business license section may file an appeal therefrom to the mayor and council within 20 days from the date of this revocation. The mayor and council shall give the operator at least 10 days' notice in advance of the date of a public hearing for the purpose of determining whether or not his business license and/or wrecker decal to operate a wrecker shall be revoked and/or cancelled. Upon hearing the facts, the mayor and council, by majority vote, may reverse, vacate, or modify the order of the business license section.
(Code 1959, § 23A-12)
1188:
The operator of any wrecker removing a private motor vehicle at the request of another person not the owner thereof, other than a city police officer on duty shall report this action to the city police along with the following information: the location of its present storage place, a description of the vehicle, the tag number and the vehicle identification number. This report shall be made by the wrecker operator by telephonic communication to the police within one (1) hour of the deposit of the vehicle at its storage point.
(Code 1959, § 23A-13)
1189:
Any person, partnership, firm, association or corporation that violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall, upon conviction in municipal court, be punished as provided in section 1-1-8 of this code. Each day's unlawful violation shall constitute a separate offense hereunder. The chief of police or his delegate shall have authority to issue citations for violations of this chapter.
(Code 1959, § 23A-14)

1192:
The following words and phrases, when used in this chapter have the meanings as set out herein:
(1) Taxicab is hereby defined to be a motor vehicle operated for hire, the destination of which is under the direction of the passenger transported therein.
(2) Highway means any of the public streets, alleys, lanes, boulevards, avenues, drives, circles, or roads of the city.
(3) Owner shall mean and include any person having control of the operation or maintenance and collection of the revenue derived from cabs.
(4) Driver and operator shall mean and include any and every person in charge of driving or operating a taxicab, as defined herein, whether as owner, agent, employee or otherwise.
(5) License shall mean the license or authority granted by the governing body to engage in the taxicab business within the city.
(6) Driver's permit means the permission granted by the governing body to a person to drive a taxicab within the city.
(7) Limousine service shall mean a service whereby a vehicle is held out for hire, including the services of the driver of said vehicle, for purposes of traveling from one destination to another for a specified fee, or is contracted for or engaged on an hourly basis. The provisions of this chapter of the Code of Ordinances are hereby made applicable to any limousine service which wishes to be located and operate within the city.
(8) Operator of taxicab business shall mean any person who shall engage in the operation of furnishing taxi or limousine service within the corporate limits of the city, whether by being physically located within the corporate limits thereof, or by actively soliciting and regularly offering service to persons located within the corporate limits. It shall not include those operations delivering passengers to the city from points exterior to the city limits.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1193:
It shall be unlawful for any taxicab to be operated within the limits of the city unless and until the owner and operator shall have complied with the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1194:
Licensees under this chapter are responsible for violations of this chapter by their vehicle operators whether such operators are direct employees or independent contractors.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1195:
(a) All businesses licensed under this chapter must have and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter to be served upon the licensee or owner may be served. This person must be a resident of Clayton County. The licensee shall file the name of such agent, along with the written consent of such agent with the city and shall be in such form as prescribed.
(b) Service of notice under this chapter shall be as follows:
(1) By delivery to the owner or registered agent personally;
(2) By registered or certified mail with postage prepaid deposited in the United States mail addressed to the owner's or occupant's last known address; or
(3) If service of notice cannot be accomplished by using the methods stated in subsections (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this section, by posting a copy of the notice in a conspicuous place on the premises of the company base of operations in the county.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1196:
Drivers shall, while on duty, practice good personal hygiene and wear proper dress while operating a vehicle for hire. Proper dress shall mean the wearing of shoes, ankle-length pants, as well as a shirt or blouse with sleeves and collar. Clothing must be clean and not visibly soiled. Licensees under this chapter are responsible for driver dress and conduct.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1197:
(a) A driver while operating a vehicle for hire is not to smoke or play a radio or tape player if objected to by a passenger.
(b) No person operating a vehicle under the provisions of this chapter shall transport or have in his possession any alcoholic beverage or illegal drug or controlled substance.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1198:
The storage or transport of hazardous material in the exterior, interior compartment, or trunk of a taxicab is prohibited.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1199:
Every taxicab driver shall inspect his or her vehicle after the departure of each passenger to ascertain that no article has been left behind. In the event that a passenger does leave an article in a cab, the driver shall immediately attempt to return it. If the driver is unable to immediately return the article, the dispatcher shall be notified and the article shall be turned in to the business office not later than the end of the driver's shift. The taxicab owner and business shall make a diligent effort to locate the owner of any lost article and shall retain the article at its business office for at least thirty (30) days.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1200:
Taxicabs shall be operated only from an established place of business, and before using the streets as parking places, operators of such taxicab must secure a permit from the city traffic engineer to park at a particular place, which permit shall not be granted except by and with the consent of adjacent property owners, and no space shall allow more than two (2) vehicles in one (1) particular locality; provided that nothing herein shall prohibit the concentration of a larger number of taxicabs at places where the public is assembled in large groups, such as baseball and football games, city auditorium, churches, schools, and like gathering places.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1201:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any taxicab operator to stop his or her taxicab for the purpose of discharging or receiving passengers except at a point as near his or her right-hand sidewalk or curb as possible.
(b) Taxicab divers carrying passengers for hire on the streets of the city shall receive and discharge passengers through the door(s) away from the vehicular portion of the streets.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1202:
Every taxicab driver shall operate his or her taxi in accordance with the laws of the state and the city, and with due regard for the safety, convenience and comfort of passengers and the general public.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1203:
(a) The governing body reserves the right to regulate the rates and fares from time to time to be charged by taxicabs and owners of taxicabs in the city.
(b) The owner and driver of every taxicab operated in the city shall have posted at a conspicuous place inside the taxicab where all passengers may see the same, the rates charged for carrying passengers and the manner of determining the fare to be charged passengers. This provision shall not be applicable to limousines.
(c) If a fare is to be determined by time or mileage or both, then the taxicab shall be equipped with a meter in good condition to record the amount to be charged on each trip, which amount shall be shown in figures visible to the passenger. The meters shall be subject to inspection from time to time by the city police department. This provision shall not be applicable to limousines.
(d) No taxicab driver shall deceive or attempt to deceive any passenger who may ride in his or her taxicab or who may desire to ride in his or her taxicab as to the destination or the rate of fare to be charged, nor shall the driver convey or cause to be conveyed any passenger to a place other than the one (1) designated by the passenger.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1204:
All business licenses, driver permits and individual vehicle stickers required by this chapter are nontransferable.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1205:
(a) Penalty for violation of chapter provisions. Any person who drives a taxicab upon the streets of the city without a permit required by this chapter or who drives a taxicab upon such streets while his or her driver's permit is suspended or revoked, or who violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor.
(b) Liability of vehicle owner. Any person who knowingly authorizes or permits a taxicab, limousine or other vehicle for hire, owned by him or her or under his or her control, to be operated for hire within the city by any person who is not authorized under this chapter, or who is not permitted under this chapter, or in violation of any of the provisions of this chapter, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Each day that a person knowingly authorizes or permits a taxicab, limousine, or other vehicle for hire, owned or operated by him or under his control, to be driven within the city by any person who is not authorized under this chapter or in or in violation of any of the provisions of this chapter shall be considered a separate violation.
(c) Revocation of driver's permit upon conviction. In addition to other penalties provided in the Charter of the city, this Code of Ordinances, and laws of the state, the judge of the municipal court of the city shall have the authority to revoke a taxicab driver's permit when the holder thereof is convicted of a violation of the Code of the Ordinances of the city.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1206:
Where there is an apparent conflict in this chapter between specific and general provisions, it is the intention hereof that the specific shall control.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1210:
No person shall operate any taxicab business within the city until the license provided for in this chapter has been granted and issued. No person shall drive a taxicab within the city without first having obtained a driver's permit as provided in this chapter. Incidental, intermittent and unscheduled passenger deliveries into the city by taxicab operators located and situated exterior to the city shall not require the driver's permit as described herein.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1211:
The chief of police shall cause an investigation to be made into the truthfulness of the information provided by the applicant and into the personal and occupational history of the applicant. The chief of police shall determine on the basis of the investigation whether the license or permit should be issued or renewed. If the chief of police decides that the license or permit should be issued or renewed, he shall immediately notify the applicant. If the chief of police decides that the permit or license should not be issued or renewed, he shall immediately notify the applicant and inform the applicant of the reasons for the denial.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1212:
(a) Grounds for suspension or revocation. A business license or driver's permit may be suspended or revoked for the following reasons:
(1) The applicant furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information or omits information requested in the application for a license or permit.
(2) Failure to pay all fees, taxes or other charges.
(3) Failure to maintain all of the general qualifications applicable to the initial issuance of a license or driver's permit.
(4) Failure to have the driver's permit posted in the taxicab in a place and manner clearly visible to all passengers at all times.
(5) Charging a fare in excess of those fares on file with the chief of police.
(6) Having four (4) or more moving traffic violations while operating any taxicab, limousine or passenger-carrying vehicle, during any twelve-month period.
(7) Refusing to accept a passenger solely on the basis of race, color, national origin, religious belief, gender or sexual orientation. Sexual orientation shall mean the state of being heterosexual, homosexual or bisexual. Operators shall not refuse to accept a passenger unless the passenger is obviously intoxicated or dangerous.
(8) Allowing the required insurance coverage to lapse or allowing a vehicle to operate in the city without an inspection sticker.
(9) For violation of any part of this chapter.
(b) Preliminary investigation; show cause hearing; findings of fact. Where it is reported to the chief of police that a business licensee or driver permittee is engaged in any conduct set forth in subsection (a) of this section, the chief of police shall conduct a preliminary investigation in order to determine whether there is a basis for the report. If his preliminary investigation reveals that there may be a basis for revocation or suspension of the license or permit, the license or permit holder shall be notified to appear before the chief of police on a date certain and show cause why the license or permit should not be revoked or suspended. The license or permit holder may appear in person at such hearing or be represented by counsel. At the conclusion of the hearing, the chief of police, based upon the evidence submitted at such hearing, shall enter an order make a finding of fact, and then:
(1) Find that the evidence does not authorize a revocation or suspension;
(2) Issue a warning to the license or permit holder;
(3) Suspend the license or permit and probate suspension;
(4) Suspend the license or permit for up to thirty (30) days; or
(5) Suspend the license or permit pending a hearing by the mayor and counsel on revocation.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1216:
(a) No owner shall operate, or allow others to operate a taxicab on the streets of Forest Park, Georgia, without first obtaining a taxicab owner's business license. The taxicab owner's business license application form will be obtained from the office of the Police Chief of Forest Park, Georgia. The application form will require the following information:
(1) Full name and address of person proposing to operate or conduct a taxicab business within the city. A statement that the applicant is twenty-one (21) years of age or older. No license to operate a taxicab business shall be granted to any person under twenty-one (21) years of age.
(2) A full and complete statement of the business to be engaged in and the type of equipment to be used.
(3) Addresses of the dispatch location or place from which the business is to be operated or conducted, the telephone switchboard location, and the parking area location for the taxicab businesses' vehicles.
(4) Whether the operator of the taxicab business for which the license is sought is a corporation, partnership, or individual.
(5) Trade name of the taxicab business to be operated.
(6) If an individual, the owner's name and home address.
(7) If a partnership, the names and addresses, including street and post office boxes, of all partners and the extent of each partner's interest.
(8) If a corporation, the names and addresses of all officers and the amount of its capital stock.
(9) General description of identifying words and color scheme of the taxicab fleet.
(10) A list of all drivers who will be scheduled for licensing under this chapter. The list must indicate whether the drivers are employees of the business or independent contractors.
(11) The make, model, year, and passenger capacity of all vehicles to be operated under the license.
(12) Name and policy number of the insurance carrier providing liability coverage for the taxicabs, as well as the amount of coverage, which in no event shall be less than the amount of coverage required under section 9-5-48 of this chapter.
(13) An affirmative statement that any business conducted under the license granted upon such application shall be in full and complete compliance with all national, state, county, municipal and local laws, ordinances, rules and regulations, with a particular reference to wages, hours, conditions of employment, and the protection by liability insurance of all persons whom the law requires the operators of such a business to protect.
(14) A copy of the rate schedule.
(15) The daily hours of operation for the business.
(16) Any and all other information as may be required by the chief of police.
(b) Upon approval by the chief of police of the taxicab owners' business license, the owner must have on record with the chief of police the original and a copy of the insurance policy of the business covering all taxicabs, evidence that the business has purchased the required business license from the city, and each taxicab to be operated must have an inspection sticker properly affixed, before beginning operation in the city.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1217:
Every person engaged in the business of conducting a taxicab business in the city shall pay to the city an annual license fee in advance for the privilege of using the streets for carrying on the same as provided in chapter 1 of this title. In addition, the license holder shall pay such business and occupation tax as provided in title 3, chapter 3.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1218:
No license to operate any taxicab business within the city shall be issued or continued in operation unless the operator of the taxicab business has in full force and effect a liability insurance policy for each taxicab in an amount that shall not be less than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) for bodily injury to any one (1) person; fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) for injuries to more than one (1) person which are sustained in the same accident; and twenty-five thousand ($25,000.00) for property damage resulting from any one (1) accident. Such insurance policy shall inure to the benefit of any person who shall be injured, or who shall sustain damage to property proximately caused by the negligence of the holder of any taxicab license, his servants, or agents. Such insurance shall be with a company authorized to do business in the state, and such insurance shall be kept in force. It shall be the duty of the chief of police of the city to enforce this requirement. Such insurance shall be subject to approval of the city, and termination of the insurance protection shall automatically operate as a revocation of the license to operate a taxicab business within the city. License holders shall file policies of insurance with the police department, and license holders shall ensure that their insurance carriers provide the city a written notice at least ten (10) days before the cancellation of any policy.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)
1221:
No driver shall operate or be allowed to operate a taxicab for hire on the streets of Forest Park, Georgia, unless the operator shall have a current and unrevoked taxicab driver's permit. The taxicab driver's permit application form will be obtained from the office of the police chief. The application form will require the following information:
(1) Name and home address of driver.

1231:
All vehicles for hire to be used by a licensee in the city shall be inspected annually and approved by the chief of police, such inspection to be made prior to the issuance or renewal of a company license. Once a vehicle meets the requirements of the inspection, a sticker will be affixed to the left side of the windshield. The requirements that each vehicle must meet are as follows:
(1) Exterior inspection. Exterior inspection shall ensure that headlights, taillights, brake lights, directional signal lights, license plate lights, windshield wipers, all vehicle glass, window cranks or electric windows, doors and door locks, trunk lid, trunk, hood, door handles, exhaust system, bumpers, fenders, body, tires and other vehicle parts are in good condition and functioning properly. The tire tread depth shall be no less than three thirty-seconds inch ( 3/32 ) on an original or retreaded tire, with no cuts or breaks in the side wall. There shall be no tears or rust holes in the vehicle body and no loose pieces hanging from the vehicle body. All vehicles for hire operated by a single company or licensee shall be painted a uniform color. There shall be no unrepaired body damage or any body condition which would create a safety problem or interfere with the operation of the vehicle.
(2) Interior inspection. Interior inspection shall include the rearview mirror, steering wheel, foot brakes, parking brakes, air conditioning and heating systems to ensure each item is in good operating condition. The upholstery, floor mats, headlining, door panels and the trunk compartment shall be inspected to ensure there are no tears, that they are clean and have no offensive odors and that the trunk has sufficient space for passenger luggage. Vehicles for hire shall have posted therein in a place plainly visible to passengers hiring such vehicle a schedule of rates, the size, form and substance of which shall be approved by the police chief.
(3) Other required features and equipment. The vehicle shall have a spare tire and jack. The spare tire shall be securely attached and in proper serviceable condition.
(4) Random inspection; removal; sticker removal; additional requirements. Vehicles shall be subject to random inspections at any time. Vehicles found to be substandard shall be removed from service immediately and shall be subject to immediate vehicle inspection sticker removal by the chief of police.
(5) Sticker proof of meeting licensing and insurance and last inspection requirements. The inspection sticker is proof that the company met the licensing and insurance requirements at the time of license issuance and that the vehicle passed the last vehicle inspection. Each vehicle operator must have in the vehicle proof of current insurance coverage. Any company or vehicle letting insurance coverage lapse shall have the inspection sticker removed by the chief of police and be subject to suspension of its business license. Business operations shall not be resumed until proof of insurance is provided to the chief of police, the license reinstated and the vehicle or vehicles reinspected and new inspection stickers issued by the chief of police.
(Ord. No. 01-05, § 1, 5-21-2001)

1305:
For the purpose of this article, the following words and phrases when used herein shall be construed as follows:
(1) Tattoo shall mean to mark or color the skin by pricking in coloring matter so as to form indelible marks or figures or by the production of scars; provided, however, that the word "tattoo" shall not mean a tattoo placed upon the skin by a physician for medical identification purposes.
(2) Tattoo artist shall mean any person who actually performs the work of tattooing.
(3) Tattoo establishment shall mean any room or place where tattooing is practiced or where the business of tattooing is conducted or any part thereof.
(4) Tattoo operator shall mean any person who controls, operates, conducts or manages any tattoo establishment, whether actually performing the work of tattooing or not.
(Code 1959, § 1SA-1)
1306:
No person shall operate a tattoo establishment or engage in the practice or business of tattooing as a tattoo operator or tattoo artist unless and until the person has first secured a license to do so from the city. Each application for a license to engage in the practice or business of tattooing as a tattoo operator or tattoo artist shall include payment of an investigative fee and an annual license fee in amounts to be determined by the governing body from time to time in a separate resolution.
(Code 1959, § 18A-2; Ord. No. 08-11, § 33, 3-17-2008; Ord. No. 26-12, § 3, 7-20-2026)
1307:
Any person desiring to operate a tattoo establishment or desiring to operate as a tattoo operator or tattoo artist shall make application for a permit to the police department, on forms supplied by that department. The minimum age of each applicant shall be eighteen (18) years of age. Fingerprints of all applicants shall be taken by the bureau. Applicants for permits shall also furnish to the detective bureau two (2) photographs showing a front and side picture of the full face of the applicant, size two and one-half (2½) inches by two and three-fourths (2¾) inches. Applicants for permits shall present to the bureau a medical certificate from a medical doctor certifying that the person is sound physically, mentally, has good eyesight and is not infected with a disease which can be communicated through openings in the human skin.
(Code 1959, § 18A-9)
1308:
All licenses granted shall be issued in the name of the individual person applying therefor, shall contain the location of the tattoo establishment where the applicant shall operate and shall not be transferable.
(Code 1959, § 18A-4)
1309:
No tattoo operator or tattoo artist shall tattoo any person who is a minor, any person who is under either the influence of alcohol, drugs or other stimulants, or depressants or any person of unsound mind.
(Code 1959, § 18A-5)
